England is considering a bid to host the UEFA Nations League finals in June as the Football Association (FA) explores the possibility of staging the competition’s final four matches. The FA has registered its interest with UEFA, joining Spain and France, which have also expressed interest in hosting the tournament. The Nations League finals, scheduled to take place between June 9 and 13, will feature the semi-finals, final and third-place play-off, with all four matches hosted by one country. According to BBC Sport on Tuesday, the FA is still discussing potential venues, with uncertainty over whether Wembley Stadium would be available for the competition. The only publicly announced events at Wembley in June are two concerts by singer Sam Fender, although they are scheduled for after the Nations League finals. England’s interest comes after Thomas Tuchel’s side secured top spot in their group with an impressive 3-2 victory over Spain in Madrid. The result means England will be seeded in Friday’s quarter-final draw, ahead of their next round of matches scheduled for March. Tuchel’s team could face Belgium, the Netherlands, Denmark or Norway in the quarter-finals, with victory potentially taking them closer to a place in the June finals. If the FA’s hosting bid is successful, it would provide England with an opportunity to stage a major international football tournament ahead of Euro 2028. The European Championship will be jointly hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland, giving the countries an opportunity to prepare for the tournament through international football events.
